title: AP/CNN: $20M Body Camera Promise Unfulfilled at Both Fatal ICE Shootings
excerpt: Reporting confirmed that neither the Houston nor Maine fatal ICE shootings involved agents wearing body cameras, despite DHS receiving $20 million from Congress for the devices and a February 2026 pledge to rapidly deploy them nationwide.
content:
Following two fatal ICE shootings in six days — Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Houston on July 7 and Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero in Biddeford, Maine on July 13 — reporting from the Associated Press and CNN revealed that agents at both scenes were not wearing body cameras.

DHS had received a $20 million congressional appropriation specifically for body camera procurement and deployment. In February 2026, then-DHS Secretary Kristi Noem had pledged to 'rapidly acquire and deploy' body cameras after two U.S. citizens were shot by federal immigration officers in Minneapolis. Yet more than five months later, the cameras had still not been issued to officers in Houston or Maine, leaving no footage of either fatal shooting from the government's perspective.

  • DHS blamed 'back-to-back Democrat shutdowns' for interrupting the body camera rollout when asked why agents lacked cameras despite the appropriated funding.
  • Congress had specifically earmarked the $20 million for body camera acquisition, and Republican Rep. Mark Amodei had confirmed that the funding was intended for that purpose.
  • The Intercept separately reported that ICE officers at the Maine shooting scene were wearing body cameras but could not activate them, as the cameras were embedded in multi-function radio mic devices officers were not trained to operate.
  • Without any body camera, dashcam, or government video from either scene, eyewitness accounts and DHS statements have directly conflicted in both cases.
